findings.title: Crash when Google Meet is the location and there is no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or `[]`, which is the normal case for users with no destination calendar set. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining (the old code used `?.integration`). When `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar exists, this throws a TypeError and `EventManager.create` fails. Previously this case fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references are no longer stored with a credentialId
findings.body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` sets the credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result. The old code stored `result.credentialId` for video results. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy. As a result, Zoom, Daily, Teams and other meetings created after this change are never deleted when the booking is cancelled. Keep `result.credentialId` for video results.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch is sent with an undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert call guards this with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. Before this change `selectedCalendar` always fell back to "primary". In this case the patch fails (its promise is not awaited or handled), so the event description is never updated with the Meet link. Apply the same `|| "primary"` fallback here.

findings.title: Fallback lookup in update/delete can never match, so destination calendar is ignored
findings.body:
In `updateEvent`, the fallback runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it then does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. That compares each calendar against a falsy value, so it effectively always returns undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. For references without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings, or references created by the paths changed in this PR), consequences are:
- `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails.
- `deleteEvent` (line 317, same pattern) targets "primary" instead of the destination calendar. It gets a 404, which is silently resolved, and the event is never deleted.

findings.title: Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId
findings.body: In the branch for destinations without a `credentialId`, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `destination.externalId`. The stored reference therefore gets `externalCalendarId: undefined`; previously `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` was stored. In addition, Google's `createEvent` now picks its calendar by `credentialId`, finds no match, and creates the event in "primary" instead of the configured destination calendar. Pass `destination.externalId`, and make the Google service honour it.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId
findings.body: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` are taken from `updateEvent` results. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets `externalId` or `credentialId`, so both are always undefined; previously they came from `evt.destinationCalendar`. `editLocationHandler` persists these as new booking references. Later cancel and update calls then fall into the legacy no-credential paths and the broken Google fallback, so events can end up on the wrong calendar or fail to update or delete.

findings.title: Other hosts' calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so for a collective event the other hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded. Those hosts never get a calendar event, which is exactly the scenario this PR aims to fix. Initialise to `[]` (or create the array before pushing) for collective events.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent filters by the main host's calendar, silently creating nothing for other hosts
findings.body: `createEvent` filters the credential's calendars to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`. For a collective event, `EventManager` now calls `createEvent` with each additional host's credential, but the filter still uses the first (main host's) calendar. The second host's CalDAV calendars never match, so `Promise.all([])` creates no object. The method still returns a success result with a uid, so the failure is invisible and the host gets no event. Select the destination by the credential being used, as the Google service does.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent uses the main host's calendar id with another host's credential
findings.body: For collective events, `createEvent` is now invoked once per host destination with that host's credential. This service still builds the URL from `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which is the main host's calendar id (possibly not even an Outlook calendar). The request to `/me/calendars/{otherId}/events` fails, so additional Office365 hosts never get the event. The service should pick the destination calendar matching the credential.

findings.title: Lark createEvent ignores which host's credential is used
findings.body: `createEvent` and `createAttendees` always use the first destination calendar's externalId. When `EventManager` creates the event for a second collective host with their Lark credential, the main host's calendar id is used with the wrong account, so creation fails. The same applies to `createAttendees` at line 164. Select the destination matching the current credential.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation runs once per reference and still deletes only one host's events
findings.body: The recurring-series deletion block is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For a collective booking with N calendar references, it iterates all organizer calendar credentials over all `updatedBookings` N times, causing duplicate delete calls. Each pass still uses `updBooking.references.find(...)` (the first calendar reference only) and only the organizer's credentials. The other hosts' recurring events are therefore never deleted from their calendars. Move the recurring logic out of the loop and iterate every calendar reference, using each reference's own credential.

findings.title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging bookings
findings.body: When `newBookingId` is given, the code does `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes a single calendar event. With multiple per-host calendar references now possible, the other hosts' old events are left behind as orphaned duplicates in their calendars.

findings.title: Each collective host gets a separate Google Meet conference
findings.body: Each host's Google calendar now receives its own `events.insert` with `conferenceData.createRequest` and `conferenceDataVersion: 1`. Google creates a new Meet conference for every inserted event, so hosts on different Google accounts see different Meet links in their calendars. Attendees receive only one link through cal.com emails, so participants can join different meetings. Only the main host's event should create the conference, and the others should reuse its link.

findings.title: Organization slug condition inverted by unrelated change
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the real slug only when billing is disabled; with billing on, only `requestedSlug` is stored until payment. The new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts this. With billing enabled, the slug is claimed immediately, bypassing the payment flow. With billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking subdomain routing. It should be `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {} : { slug }`.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changes from object to array
findings.body: `CalendarEvent` objects are spread directly into webhook payloads (cancel, reject, reschedule-request, etc.). Changing `destinationCalendar` from an object to an array is a breaking change for external webhook consumers such as Zapier and custom integrations, which read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The value is also now inconsistent: `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED and `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED, as the e2e test shows. Consider keeping the external payload shape stable, or document and version the change.

findings.title: No tests for multi-host destination calendar behavior
findings.body: The PR reworks event creation, update and cancellation for multiple calendar references, adds DB credential lookups, and changes the `Calendar.createEvent` signature. The only test change is updating one webhook expectation to `[]`. Nothing covers the collective multi-host path or the regressions above, such as the Meet-without-destination crash or missing video credentialId. Unit tests for `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` and the cancel flow with multiple references are needed.
